notices.trigger: Only a consumer transaction the consumer did not solicit, resulting from direct contact by the supplier at a place other than the supplier's permanent place of business, with a cash sales price of at least $25
notices.support: The trigger is in the definition, IC 24-5-10-4: "a consumer transaction that the consumer did not solicit that results from the direct contact by a supplier at a place other than the supplier's permanent place of business."
notices.summary_row: Home solicitation sales: whole chapter (trigger, three business days, two-copy separate 10 point bold notice)
notices.hold_reason: The only block is the whole of IC 24-5-10 (eighteen sections), and the chapter prescribes no sentence, only a form (two copies, separate document, 10 point bold) and five content items, so there is no notice wording to copy.

notices.title: Notice of the contractor's right to offer to cure construction defects

notices.format: Conspicuous capitals notice in substantially the statutory form; may be included in the contract; no type size stated
notices.support: The notice must be conspicuous and may be included as part of the underlying contract signed by the home owner.
notices.summary_row: Notice of right to offer to cure construction defects (capitals notice, may be in the contract)

changes.new: Three business days (IC 24-5-11-10.6, every home improvement contract over $150 since July 1, 2017; IC 24-5-10, unsolicited home sales)
changes.support: Every Indiana home improvement contract over $150 since July 1, 2017 must be accompanied by the fixed statement

changes.new: Every home improvement contract over $150 entered into after June 30, 2017, whether or not door to door (IC 24-5-11-10.6); also home sales the consumer did not solicit, made away from the supplier's permanent place of business (IC 24-5-10)
changes.support: This is not limited to door-to-door sales.

changes.new: Counted to midnight of the third business day after the later of signing by both parties or, if applicable, the date the consumer receives the insurer's final determination of coverage (IC 24-5-11-10.6); business day excludes Sunday and legal holidays, so Saturday counts.
changes.support: "Business day" (24-5-10-1) "means a day other than Sunday or a legal holiday", so Saturday counts.

changes.new: IC 32-27-3: construction or substantial remodeling of a residence (remodeling over 50 percent of assessed value); notice of claim at least 60 days before suit, contractor's response within 21 days
changes.support: Notice of claim "At least sixty (60) days before filing"; contractor's written response "Within twenty-one (21) days after service"

changes.new: 24-5-11-10.6 statement of right to cancel and duplicate NOTICE OF CANCELLATION (every home improvement contract over $150 since July 1, 2017; 24-5-10 only for unsolicited home sales) and 32-27-3 defect process
changes.support: IC 24-5-11-10.6 gives EVERY home improvement contract "entered into by a real property improvement supplier and a consumer after June 30, 2017" its own fixed-text statement and NOTICE OF CANCELLATION, whether or not the sale was door to door.

unsure: IN-cancel-10-6: the statement and form are required in every home improvement contract over $150, so it should print for every contract, but the whole section is the only block and holds non-notice subsections, so it is held.

IN-cure: needed only for construction or substantial remodeling (over 50 percent of assessed value), which the builder cannot tell; the file says the notice is owed upon entering the contract, so it may belong in every residential contract.
IN-cancel: chapter 10 prescribes no wording; whether the 10.6 form also satisfies chapter 10 for an unsolicited home sale is not stated in the file.
